entries.subject: DAMIT 1797: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-1797.txt. Model 1797, version 2017-06-13, pole (19°, 21°), period 5.981768 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 160 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: DAMIT documentation
entries.finding: [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/pages/documentation) — coordinate units, pole, period and diameter semantics. CC BY 4.0.

entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. (2017), Volumes and bulk densities of forty asteroids from ADAM shape modeling](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A%26A...601A.114H) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: Marchis et al. (2013), Characteristics and large bulk density of the C-type main-belt triple asteroid (93) Minerva
entries.finding: [Marchis et al. (2013), Characteristics and large bulk density of the C-type main-belt triple asteroid (93) Minerva](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013Icar..224..178M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the selected archive model has a physical size calibration. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 147.1 ± 2.24 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 93 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model publication supporting DAMIT 1797
entries.finding: The live DAMIT model-to-reference export binds selected model 1797 to Volumes and bulk densities of forty asteroids from ADAM shape modeling (2017). That publication supports the selected reconstruction. The imported entry conflated three surveys; listing them together did not establish three usable models or a registered reflectance mosaic.

entries.subject: Hanuš et al. 2018
entries.finding: [Hanuš et al. 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.06116) and [occultation dimensions](https://www.asteroidoccultation.com/observations/Asteroid_Dimensions_from_Occultations.html) — size comparison candidates; an independent fit or occultation ellipsoid is not silently equated with this mesh’s volume.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: The survey found no alternative archive solution for this target.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.
